svg.text: HICS IESH v0.2
Perfboard placement
BLANK PY-10CM*15CM board, 57 x 37 holes at 2.54 mm. Zoned placement, separation rules and order of work - not a hole-exact route.
ANALOGUE
DIGITAL
2 x 1x20 FEMALE HEADER STRIPS -> Pi GPIO
BODIES ON THE UNDERSIDE, tails soldered on top - it seats DOWN onto the Pi. upper
row = Pi ODD pins 1-39, lower row = Pi EVEN pins 2-40. MARK PIN 1.
GND RAIL flood one continuous strip - tie to at least TWO Pi GND pins (6, 9, 14, 20, 25, 30, 34, 39)
+3.3 V RAIL from Pi pins 1 and 17 - MCP3208 VDD+VREF, I2C trio, pull-ups, DHT22, soil, raindrop
+5 V RAIL from the POWER terminal via the LM2596 @ 5.00 V - MQ HEATERS ONLY. do NOT wire this rail to Pi pins 2/4
MCP3208 DIP-16
pin 1 top-left. 16->3V3 VDD 15->3V3 VREF
14+9->GND 13->pin23 CLK 12->pin21 Dout
11->pin19 Din 10->pin24 CS
C1 100 nF
across the ADC supply pins,
as close as it will go
MQ DIVIDERS R3 R4 (MQ-7 -> CH0) R5 R6 (MQ-135 -> CH1)
AOUT -> node -> GND, node -> CHx. USE MATCHED PAIRS and put the
measured (R1+R2)/R2 into sensors/config.py:26
on the 5 V rail beside the
MQ feed. WATCH POLARITY
I2C BREAKOUT BMP280 0x76 · OLED 0x3C · DS3231 0x68
shortest run on the board. route SDA and SCL side by side with a GND between them. do
NOT add pull-ups - the Pi 3B+ already has 1k8
R1 4k7
1-WIRE pull-up: GPIO4 (pin 7) -> 3V3
R2 4k7
DHT22 pull-up: GPIO23 (pin 16) -> 3V3.
CHECK the module first - U6
FREE ADC CHANNELS CH3 CH4 CH5 CH6 CH7
raindrop x2 and LDR x4 are owned and unfitted - leave room, fit after gate 6
SCREW TERMINALS 14 ways - MAST 8 | SOIL 4 | POWER 2
cables leave the board at this edge, nearest the glands. LABEL EVERY WAY ON THE BOARD IN INDELIBLE PEN
grid 142 x 91 mm (57 x 37 holes @ 2.54 mm) on a 150 x 100 mm board. COUNT YOUR OWN BOARD - vendors vary by a hole or two at the edges.
The 65 x 70 carrier-hat-v1 footprint is deliberately NOT matched: the corrected box takes the full board flat, and a HAT may overhang the Pi. Zones transfer to the real PCB; the outline does not.
LAYOUT RULES
1. Analogue apart from digital
MCP3208 and the MQ dividers on the left; I2C and the
DHT22 pull-up on the right. A switching MQ heater beside
an ADC input is a measurable error, not a theoretical
one.
2. One continuous ground
Flood the GND row into a single strip and tie it to at
least TWO Pi GND pins. A thin shared return is a classic
cause of fault F2.
3. I2C as short as physically possible
Plus 100 kHz instead of 400 kHz in config.txt. Do NOT add
pull-ups - the Pi 3B+ already has 1k8 on GPIO2/GPIO3.
4. Rails before components, and buzz them
Header, ground strip and supply rails first. Then meter
GND/3V3/5V against each other - ALL THREE MUST READ OPEN
- before the board ever meets the Pi.
5. Label every terminal on the board itself
The masking-tape flags on the demo build are the reason a
rebuild was needed at all.
6. Iron under three seconds per pad
Cheap phenolic board lifts pads if you dwell. ~350 C, in
and out.
ORDER OF WORK
both header strips, all 40 tails soldered. Mark pin 1
GND rail, flooded, to >= 2 Pi GND pins
+3.3 V rail from Pi pins 1 and 17
+5 V rail - NOT connected to Pi pins 2/4
GATE
GND / 3V3 / 5V all OPEN to each other, board OFF the Pi
MCP3208 + C1
R1 R2 pull-ups, R3-R6 dividers, C2
screw terminals, every way labelled in pen
onto the Pi. tests/test_all.py, one sensor at a time
Generated by scripts/gen_drawings.py - edit ZONES there, not this SVG. Placement is deliberate; hole-exact routing is yours to finish on the board.
